resource_visual_inspection.source: Data/GameInter.wil direct pixel inspection; exported at native size and enlarged with nearest-neighbor for review

frames.visual_description: scroll/parchment quest panel with the two baked English section labels and right-side operation-icon area
frames.note: These are artwork labels; they do not by themselves prove the runtime field names or click behavior.

frames.visual_description: blank parchment/detail panel intended to receive runtime-selected quest body text

frames.visual_description: right-pointing arrow operation icon on a circular tan base: Frame 723 renders the arrow in bright green (106 green pixels, sample RGB (192,236,72)), Frame 724 in muted gold (0 green pixels, sample RGB (112,88,72))
frames.note: WILSDK decode (28x28, bbox (0,0,27,27) both frames); earlier 'Frame 724 empty' claim came from the retired hand-rolled WIL parser and is superseded.

hit_rects.basis: Shared control constructor 0x00417550 selects the GameInter frame and writes SetRect from the frame width/height.

scroll_semantics.this+0x58: list scroll offset (rows); painted row index = row - this+0x58; click in list area increments with clamp [0, this+0x5C-1] (0x0044888B-0x0044889E), wheel decrements with floor 0 (0x00448761-0x00448774)
scroll_semantics.this+0x5C: list row count clamp; written by Paint each frame at 0x00447DED from the decoded row counter
scroll_semantics.paint_guard: rows outside [this+0x58, this+0x58+19) are skipped (0x004475CE-0x004475E1 and 0x0044765C-0x00447670)

hit_rect.source: SetRect via USER32 IAT [0x4762B0] at 0x004487CC with window.x+0x50, window.y+0x136, window.x+0xFA, window.y+0x17C

scroll_semantics.this+0x60: detail body scroll offset (lines); click inside the body hit rect increments with clamp [0,3] (0x0044884D-0x00448860), wheel decrements with floor 0 (0x00448728-0x0044873A)

paint_order.evidence: The paint entry calls the window vtable +0x0C before quest-specific controls or text processing.
The two child controls are positioned at window-relative (290,59) and (290,89), then their vtable +0x04 paint slots are called.
The list cursor is refreshed, records are decoded through 0x45E0C0, long/short entries are selected, and visible rows are emitted at the 15-pixel cadence.
When the detail field exists, Frame 705 is looked up and drawn at window-relative origin (65,294), after the list update path.
The detail field is decoded and only three lines in the this+0x60 window are emitted through 0x45DD70 at window-relative (80,310), 15 pixels apart.

event_dispatch.evidence: The global UI dispatcher calls the quest input handler and dispatches the handled result through the quest window slot.
The update dispatcher calls the quest navigation handler, which refreshes both child controls and list state.

confirmed: Frame 700 and the two control frame pairs are statically tied to the quest window constructor.
The quest list is read through 0x0045E0C0 and rendered with a 15-pixel row cadence.
Both operation controls are repositioned by 0x00447470 using the same relative coordinates.
Frame 705 is selected by the task refresh path for the detail/body text region.
The quest window's local paint sequence is statically ordered from base, controls, list rows, selected detail frame and body text.
Row geometry is window.x+65, window.y+90+15*row with a 19-row paint window; the list scroll offset is this+0x58 with row-count clamp this+0x5C (written by Paint each frame).
Detail body geometry is window.x+80, window.y+310, 15px apart, 3 visible lines, hit rect (80,310)-(250,380) window-relative; body scroll offset is this+0x60 clamped to [0,3].
Mouse wheel (0x00448700) decrements both scroll offsets with floor 0; mouse click (0x00448780) increments them with the clamps above.
Frame 705 is a full-coverage 204x76 detail panel (WIL bbox (0,0,202,76)) drawn at (65,294), sized to hold the three 15px body lines.
Frame pairs are pixel-verified: 721 green X / 722 gold X; 723 green right-arrow / 724 gold right-arrow (green = highlighted, gold = normal).

Event/message twins 0x418 (mark-selected action, gated on record+0x20C==0) and 0x419 (row click with empty body at record+0x220) are built by 0x00451A10/0x00451A40 through the shared builder 0x00452940.
pending: Exact quest field separator character and any client-side pixel wrap: fields are fetched through the record vtable (0x0045E0C0: vtable +0x44 fetch, +0x68 advance) with type gates 0xA0/0xC8, and lines are emitted as discrete fields at the fixed 15px cadence, so no client wrap constant is statically visible; the separator lives in the record class and needs a runtime capture.

Business names for events 0x418 / 0x419 and for the 721-724 controls: the control-to-event chains and iconography (X = abandon/delete, arrow = next/advance) are closed, but the message IDs are not present in any local server source and user-facing names need a protocol reference or runtime capture.
